uncited: All methods in this family build on [Specific Model Architectures](8585-specific-model-architectures.md) but diverge in how the geometric information is integrated into the optimization loop.
The shared mechanism involves augmenting the standard photometric loss with geometric terms or modifying the ray sampling process to respect geometric boundaries.
Many methods introduce explicit loss terms that penalize deviations from geometric priors.
Instead of uniform or hierarchical sampling along the entire ray, these methods use depth priors to concentrate samples near the estimated surface.
This reduces computational cost and mitigates the "transparent" artifacts common in standard NeRF when geometry is ambiguous.
Some variants replace the volumetric density $\sigma$ with a Signed Distance Field (SDF).

The rendering integral is modified to integrate weights based on the SDF value relative to a truncation distance $tr$, effectively creating a thin shell around the surface rather than a volumetric blob.
